title: The grapes
subtitle: Blends of five grapes
objectives: Name Bordeaux's red and white grapes

steps.title: Reds
steps.body: Bordeaux's reds blend Merlot, the most planted grape, about 60% of red vines, Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Franc, and small amounts of Petit Verdot, Malbec and Carmenère. Since 2021, a few heat-tolerant grapes like Touriga Nacional can be used in small amounts, under trial rules.

steps.title: Why blend
steps.body: Each grape ripens at a different time and suits different soils. Merlot ripens early and likes cool clay; Cabernet Sauvignon ripens late and needs warm gravel; Cabernet Franc adds perfume. In a difficult year, blending lets the winemaker lean on whichever grape did best. Whites blend Sauvignon Blanc and Sémillon, sometimes Muscadelle.

steps.prompt: Match each grape to its role.
steps.explanation: Each grape fills a gap in the blend.

steps.body: Bordeaux labels rarely name grapes. The appellation tells you: Left Bank wines lean on Cabernet Sauvignon, Right Bank wines on Merlot.

steps.prompt: Cabernet Sauvignon is Bordeaux's most planted red grape.
steps.explanation: Not true. Merlot is the most planted, about 60% of red vines.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon and Cabernet Franc lead the reds
Blending spreads risk and balances flavour
Whites blend Sauvignon Blanc and Sémillon
